title: Indonesian Diaspora Living Abroad: The Complete Guide
summary: Everything you need to know about the Indonesian diaspora living abroad, from moving overseas to staying connected with home. A practical, heartfelt guide.
body_markdown:
[Living Abroad](https://blog.transfez.com/en/living-abroad/)


So you are thinking about making the big move. Maybe you have already packed your bags, or maybe you are still at the daydreaming stage, scrolling through photos of a new city while sipping your *kopi* at home. Either way, you are not alone. Millions of Indonesians have walked this exact path before you, building lives, careers, and communities far from *tanah air* . The **Indonesian diaspora living abroad** is one of the largest and most vibrant in Southeast Asia, and understanding what that journey really looks like can save you a lot of stress and guesswork. If you want a head start, check out this guide on[Indonesian Diaspora: Who They Are and Why They Matter](https://blog.transfez.com/en/indonesian-diaspora-who-they-are-and-why-they-matter/) before we dive in.


This article is for anyone who is curious, excited, nervous, or all three at once. We will cover why Indonesians move abroad, where they tend to go, what challenges to expect, and how to set yourself up for a smooth and fulfilling life overseas.

##


**Who Makes Up the Indonesian Diaspora?**


The Indonesian diaspora is a beautifully diverse group. You will find students chasing world-class degrees, professionals climbing corporate ladders, skilled workers sending money home to their families, entrepreneurs building businesses, and retirees enjoying a slower pace of life somewhere new.


###


**1. Students Studying Abroad**


Education is one of the biggest pull factors. Indonesian students flock to universities in Singapore, Australia, the Netherlands, the United States, and beyond. The goal is usually a degree that opens doors back home or a career path in a new country. If you are considering this route, a thorough read of[How to Study Abroad from Indonesia](https://blog.transfez.com/en/how-to-study-abroad-from-indonesia/) will give you a solid foundation.


###


**2. Skilled Workers and Professionals**


Engineers, doctors, nurses, IT specialists, and finance professionals are among the most common Indonesian workers overseas. Countries like Singapore, Saudi Arabia, Japan, South Korea, and Malaysia actively recruit Indonesian talent. Landing a job abroad takes preparation, but the career growth can be significant.


###


**3. Migrant Workers**


Hundreds of thousands of Indonesians work in domestic, hospitality, and manufacturing roles across Asia and the Middle East. These workers are the backbone of many families back home, sending remittances that support education, healthcare, and daily needs for their loved ones.


###


**4. Long-Term Settlers and Mixed-Family Households**


Some Indonesians marry locals abroad, gain permanent residency, or simply fall in love with a place and decide to stay. Over time, they build deep roots, raise children, and become part of the fabric of their adopted country while keeping their Indonesian identity alive.


##


**Why Do Indonesians Choose to Move Abroad?**


The reasons are as varied as the people themselves, but a few themes come up again and again when you talk to members of the diaspora.


###


**1. Better Career and Income Opportunities**


Higher salaries, more structured career ladders, and exposure to global industries are major draws. For many professionals, working abroad is the fastest way to level up both financially and professionally.


###


**2. World-Class Education**


Access to top-ranked universities and research institutions motivates thousands of Indonesian students every year. A degree from a well-known international institution can significantly boost your career prospects both overseas and back home.


###


**3. A New Life Experience**


Some people simply want to experience the world. Living in a different country teaches you things no classroom can, from adaptability and language skills to a genuinely global perspective on life.


###


**4. Family and Personal Ties**


Joining a spouse, parent, or sibling who is already abroad is another common path. Family reunification is a quiet but powerful driver behind a large portion of the diaspora.


##


**Top Destinations for Indonesians Living Abroad**


Where do most Indonesians end up? The answer depends a lot on your goals, but certain countries consistently top the list.


###


**1. Singapore**


Proximity to home, a strong job market, and a large existing Indonesian community make Singapore the go-to destination for many. Whether you are looking to study or work, Singapore offers a relatively smooth transition. You can read a full breakdown in this guide on[How to Work in Singapore](https://blog.transfez.com/en/how-to-work-in-singapore/) .


###


**2. Malaysia**


Shared language roots and cultural similarities make Malaysia a comfortable first step abroad for many Indonesians. The job market is active, and the cost of living is manageable.


###


**3. Saudi Arabia and the Middle East**


The Gulf region remains one of the largest employers of Indonesian migrant workers. Domestic work, construction, and hospitality are the main sectors, and many workers send a significant portion of their earnings home.


###


**4. Australia, the Netherlands, and the United States**


These destinations attract Indonesian students and highly skilled professionals. They often require more preparation in terms of visas and credentials recognition, but they offer strong long-term opportunities.


##


**Practical Steps to Prepare for Life Abroad**


Moving abroad is not something you do on a whim. Here is a practical checklist to get you started on the right foot.


1. **Sort your visa early.** Every country has different requirements, processing times, and document checklists. Do not leave this to the last minute. A beginner-friendly breakdown can be found in[How to Get a Visa: A Complete Guide for Beginners](https://blog.transfez.com/en/how-to-get-a-visa/) .
2. **Research your destination thoroughly.** Cost of living, cultural norms, local laws, and community networks all matter. Join Facebook groups and forums run by Indonesians in your target country.
3. **Set up your finances.** Open a local bank account as soon as you land. Understand how to send money home efficiently, because supporting family back in Indonesia is a reality for many diaspora members.
4. **Build your community.** Look for Indonesian student associations, mosque communities, church groups, or professional networks in your city. These connections are lifesavers, especially in the early months.
5. **Learn the local language.** Even basic proficiency in the local language shows respect and opens doors. Do not rely entirely on English unless you are in a fully English-speaking country.
6. **Stay on top of legal requirements.** Visas expire. Work permits need renewal. Health insurance is mandatory in many countries. Stay organized and set reminders for important dates.


##


**Staying Connected to Home While Living Abroad**


One of the most emotionally challenging parts of diaspora life is the distance from family and familiar culture. Here is how many Indonesians keep that connection alive.


- Regular video calls with family, especially during *Lebaran* , *Natal* , and other Indonesian celebrations.
- Cooking Indonesian food at home. Finding *tempe* , *sambal* , and *kecap manis* in international supermarkets has never been easier.
- Joining local Indonesian cultural events and diaspora organizations that celebrate Indonesian arts, food, and traditions.
- Sending remittances home to support family. Knowing how to[transfer money from abroad to Indonesia](https://blog.transfez.com/en/how-to-transfer-money-from-abroad-to-indonesia/) reliably and efficiently is a must-know skill for anyone in the diaspora.
- Staying engaged with Indonesian news, podcasts, and online communities to maintain a sense of belonging.


**See Also:**[Working Abroad: The Complete Beginner’s Guide](https://blog.transfez.com/en/working-abroad-complete-beginners-guide/)


Living abroad as part of the Indonesian diaspora is one of the most rewarding adventures you can take, but it works best when you go in with your eyes wide open. Know your reasons, do your homework, build your community, and never forget where you come from. Whether you are chasing a dream degree, a career breakthrough, or simply a new chapter, the path is well-worn by millions of Indonesians who came before you. You have got this, and a whole global community is ready to welcome you in.
